what: `--kind all` write-ordering omits a pre-write gate before the first filesystem mutation
scenario_or_breakage: The plan sequences pack-in-memory then Makefile write + partition validation then assignments JSON (plan.txt:49-53). Python abort conditions (zero `python-tests` rows, `--n-python-shards` mismatch; plan.txt:58-59,159-163) and harness hard gates (no harness rows, `untimed_targets`; rebalance.py:441-474) are documented separately but not bound to run before step 1 of that write sequence. A refactor that validates the Python leg after `write_shards` can leave a modified Makefile on disk when the Python leg aborts, violating the partition-failure invariant (Makefile-only revert; plan.txt:52,167) and the issue requirement that python shard-count mismatch abort before writes (plan.txt:10).
suggested_fix: Add an explicit `--kind all` pre-write gate subsection before plan.txt:49-53: finish baseline fetch + medians + harness `untimed_targets` / no-row checks + python `observed_shard_count` / zero-row checks + in-memory packing for both legs; exit non-zero before any `write_shards` or assignments write when any gate fails.
